title: Fabrication of Biologically Derived Injectable Materials for Myocardial Tissue Engineering
protocol: Wash porcine pericardium in deionized (DI) water for 30 minutes.
Stir porcine pericardium continuously in 1% SDS in phosphate buffered saline (PBS) for 24 hours.
Rinse porcine pericardium under running DI water after the SDS treatment.
Wash human pericardia in DI water for 30 minutes.
Stir human pericardia continuously in 1% SDS in PBS for 60-65 hours.
Rinse human pericardia under running DI water after the SDS treatment.
Remove a small piece of decellularized tissue and fresh freeze it in O.C.T. freezing medium.
Take 10 μm tissue sections every 100 μm throughout the sample for examination via histological analysis.
Examine tissue sections using hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stains to verify absence of nuclei.
Fix tissue sections, rehydrate, rinse in water, stain with Hoescht 33342 (1.0 μg/mL) for 10 minutes, then rinse well and store in the dark.
Use Qiagen DNeasy Blood and Tissue kit to quantify total DNA content of the sample.
Freeze decellularized samples with liquid nitrogen or store at -80°C.
Lyophilize samples until completely dry.
Grind dried ECM into a fine powder using a Wiley Mini Mill.
Choose the appropriate sieve size for milling; use 40 gauge mesh here.
Remove collection jar containing milled ECM powder once most of the sample has passed through the filter.
Extract remaining small sample from mill using a Q-tip or similar tool.
Ensure that both the mill and sample are clean and totally dry before milling.
Digest ECM powder with pepsin to form injectable ECM.
Use sterile vials and weigh spoons for preparation.
Filter all solutions before use to maintain sterility.
Weigh out the desired amount of ECM powder into an appropriate scintillation vial.
Add 0.1 M HCl to pepsin such that it is at a concentration of 1 mg/ml.
Ensure pepsin solution is fully dissolved by vortexing if necessary.
Add the pepsin/HCl solution to the scintillation vial with ECM powder so that ECM is at a concentration of 10 mg/ml.
Stir the solution continuously for 60-65 hours, periodically scraping down the sides of the vial.
Adjust pH to physiological level to inactivate pepsin and maintain ECM integrity.
Add 1 M NaOH to the solution in a volume that is 1/10 of the original sample.
Test the pH and adjust with small amounts (2-10 μL) of either NaOH or HCl until the desired pH (7.4) is achieved.
Keep track of all adjustments made during neutralization.
Add 10x PBS to the solution in a volume that is 1/9 of the current sample volume.
Determine the concentration of the injectable ECM and then add 1x PBS as needed to reach the final desired concentration, which is 6 mg/mL.
Prepare a 10 mM solution of biotin for tagging the ECM.
Add Biotin to the injectable ECM at a ratio of 0.3 mg/mg of ECM or use 40 μL of biotin per 1 mL of ECM if injecting at a concentration of 6 mg/mL.
Keep the biotin-ECM solution on ice for at least 1 hour prior to injection.
All processing steps can be performed at room temperature.
To prevent gelling during pH adjustment, perform this step on ice.
Anesthetize the rat using isoflurane at 5%.
Intubate the animal using an otoscope.
Maintain anesthesia at 2.5% isoflurane throughout surgery.
Add artificial tear ointment to protect the animal's eyes from dryness and hair.
Administer 3 mL of Lactated Ringers solution for hydration via subcutaneous injection in the lower abdominal area.
Place the animal in a supine position on the surgical table.
Tape down the limbs gently to secure the animal.
Use clippers to remove hair on the abdomen.
Vacuum free hair before scrubbing.
Scrub three times with betadine, starting in the middle and moving outward.
Repeat scrubbing with 70% ethanol.
Cover the animal using a surgical drape with a pre-made circular window.
Make a 3-4 cm incision from the xyphoid process to the lower right-hand side of the abdomen.
Dissect vertically down through the muscle to the right, avoiding the large vessel on the right.
Cut laterally through the muscle with scissors, exposing the diaphragm.
Be careful to avoid the liver during dissection.
Drive one needle through the xyphoid process using a 36 inch length of 3-0 Vicrile suture and hemostats.
Pull the suture halfway through and tape the ends together.
Fix the taped suture to a point above and behind the animal, lifting the xyphoid up.
Use another 36 inch length of 3-0 Vicrile suture to drive a needle through the muscle closest to the xyphoid process.
Pull through and fix the ends to a point to the right of the surgical table, fully exposing the surgical cavity.
With rat tooth microforceps, grab the center of the diaphragm and pull it out toward you.
Make a very small incision with blunt scissors at the center of the diaphragm, avoiding the lungs.
Visualize the heart through the exposed diaphragm.
Make a 2-3 cm vertical incision through the diaphragm to further visualize the heart.
Insert a 3-inch Q-tip to the left of the cavity to push the lungs out of the way.
Secure the Q-tip with a towel clamp.
Use another Q-tip to move the right lung out of the way to locate the pericardial sac.
Tear through the pericardial sac using microforceps and large serrated forceps to expose the heart apex.
Grasp the apex of the heart with rat tooth microforceps.
Inject liquid matrix material a third of the way up from the apex, inserting the needle parallel to the epicardial surface.
Ensure the beveled edge of the needle is to the left and avoid the great cardiac vein.
Wait a few seconds before removing the needle.
Observe tissue whitening at the injection site.
Clean blood in the cavity.
Remove the towel clamp and Q-tip holding the right lung.
Use curved microhemostats and rat tooth microforceps to close the diaphragm.
Make an initial knot with the suture material.
Close the diaphragm continuously using serrated forceps and microhemostats.
Insert PE160 suction tubing before closing entirely.
Evacuate chest cavity air with a 10 mL syringe as the suture is tightened.
Ensure the diaphragm is concave after evacuation and suturing.
Turn down isoflurane to 1%.
Remove both 3-0 Vicrile sutures holding the cavity open.
Hydrate the muscle layer with sterile water, wiping excess away with a Q-tip or sterile gauze.
Close the muscle layer with intermittent sutures using a new length of 3-0 suture.
Turn off isoflurane completely.
Clean the surgical area with sterile water.
Use staples to close the skin incision.
If staples interfere with study, use 5-0 proline suture and a reverse cutting needle to close the skin with intermittent sutures.
Apply surgical glue over the closed incision site.
Anoint the incision site with triple-antibiotic ointment using a Q-tip.
Allow the animal to recover under 100% oxygen.
Remove the trachea tube when the animal starts breathing around the ventilator.
Return the animal to its home cage on a sterile towel once it is sternal.
Administer a subcutaneous injection of 0.05 mg/kg buprenorphine hydrochloride for pain relief.
Observe animals post-operatively.
Euthanize animals at specified time points.
Remove hearts for analysis.
Take short axis cross sections of hearts.
Stain sections with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) for gross tissue analysis.
Visualize injected region as pink, fibrous network in early stages.
Observe influx of cells and degradation of injected matrix over 2 to 3 weeks.
Label ECM with biotin before injection if applicable.
Stain biotin-labeled sections with HRP-conjugated streptavidin for visualization.
Perform immunohistochemical staining on slides.
Co-stain slides with FITC-conjugated isolectin for endothelial cells.
Use anti-smooth muscle actin antibody and Alexafluor secondary antibody for SMCs.
If the injection is successful, the region around the needle tip whitens and a small bolus is visible.
Carefully close the diaphragm during suturing after injection.
Ensure the diaphragm appears tight against the lungs and concave when properly closed.
Inspect for any areas where the diaphgram balloons out to indicate air left in the lungs.
Examine histology at an early time point (30 minutes to 4 hours post-injection) for a pink, fibrous area devoid of cells.
Expect to see the reassembled matrix material post-injection as a sign of successful injection location.
Observe that the network may spread interstitially and be present throughout many sections.
Consider that seeing only a very small area of matrix gel might indicate partial misdirection of the injection.
